C1.whatIsNew: A double-blind, sham-controlled RCT (N=180, 12 weeks) of an unnamed neuromodulation device found no benefit over identical-appearing sham on THI (between-group difference 1.4 points, p=0.43). The new information is a well-sized null result, not a new treatment effect.
C1.primaryEndpoint: Not reported explicitly; THI change at 12 weeks is the outcome given in the record
C1.numericalResult: THI change: device −15.2 points, sham −13.8 points; between-group difference 1.4 points (95% CI −2.1 to 4.9), p=0.43
C1.loudnessEffect: none — no psychoacoustic loudness matching or loudness rating was reported; the record contains only THI, which is a distress measure and cannot be read as loudness.
C1.distressEffect: none — THI fell in both arms but the between-group difference was 1.4 points (95% CI −2.1 to 4.9, p=0.43), i.e. no advantage over sham.
C1.clinicalSignificance: The between-group difference of 1.4 THI points, with a confidence interval spanning from −2.1 to 4.9, is far too small to matter to patients; the similar drop in the sham arm suggests the within-group improvement reflects placebo/natural course rather than the device.
mainLimitations: The record does not state the pre-specified primary endpoint, randomization method, allocation concealment details, or blinding-integrity checks
No loudness or psychoacoustic outcome reported, so nothing can be said about the tinnitus percept itself
No safety or adverse-event data reported
No follow-up beyond 12 weeks reported
Manufacturer-funded with two author-employees, which is a concern in either direction for a null trial
The device is identified only as 'neuromodulation device X', so the result cannot be mapped to a specific product in the database
Inference: the summary record is brief and may omit secondary outcomes or subgroup analyses present in the full paper
C1.conflictOfInterest: manufacturer-funded / author equity — funded by the device manufacturer and two authors are manufacturer employees; note that a null result despite sponsor involvement is somewhat reassuring about reporting bias here.
C1.weeklyTitle: Sham-controlled trial of a neuromodulation device finds no benefit over sham on tinnitus distress
C1.whyMatters: In a 180-person trial, people using the real device and people using a dummy device improved by almost exactly the same amount, so the improvement cannot be credited to the device. Negative results like this help stop ineffective devices from being promoted on the basis of before-and-after numbers alone.
C1.factuallyVerifiedReason: Every number and design feature reported here (N=180, double-blind, identical-appearing sham, 12 weeks, THI −15.2 vs −13.8, difference 1.4, 95% CI −2.1 to 4.9, p=0.43, manufacturer funding, two employee authors, peer-reviewed journal with PMID) is stated verbatim in the primary record; items absent from the record are marked 'Not reported'.
C1.summaryForAdmin: Well-sized double-blind, sham-controlled RCT (N=180) of an unnamed neuromodulation device reporting a clearly null result on THI (1.4-point between-group difference, p=0.43), despite both arms improving ~14-15 points — a textbook illustration of why within-group change is not evidence of efficacy. Manufacturer-funded with two employee authors; no loudness outcome and no safety data in the record. Flagged major so the device can be identified and, if it corresponds to a rated treatment, its distress rating and evidence score reviewed downward.

The new information is essentially a negative primary result for this drug.
C2.population: Adults with chronic tinnitus (further characteristics not reported); a post-hoc subgroup had high-frequency hearing loss
C2.secondaryEndpoints: Loudness VAS (reported for a post-hoc subgroup with high-frequency hearing loss)
C2.numericalResult: Primary endpoint TFI change at week 8: p=0.21 (not significant). Secondary loudness VAS in post-hoc subgroup with high-frequency hearing loss: p=0.03. N=90.
C2.loudnessEffect: limited — the only loudness signal is a nominal p=0.03 on a VAS in a post-hoc subgroup, which is hypothesis-generating and not evidence that the drug reduces the tinnitus percept.
C2.distressEffect: none — the pre-specified distress endpoint (TFI at week 8) was not significant (p=0.21).
C2.clinicalSignificance: No clinically meaningful benefit is demonstrated: the trial failed its primary distress endpoint, and no effect sizes or responder data are reported for the post-hoc loudness finding, so patient-relevant benefit cannot be judged.

Blinding not described in the record

C2.factuallyVerifiedReason: Every reported fact — design, N=90, primary endpoint and p=0.21, post-hoc subgroup loudness VAS p=0.03, independent academic funding, peer-reviewed with PMID — is stated in the primary record; items absent from the record (blinding, safety, demographics) are marked 'Not reported'.

Funding is independent academic and the paper is peer-reviewed with a PMID, which makes it a credible negative data point. No score or rank change; worth logging so the post-hoc loudness signal is not later cited as evidence of loudness reduction.
